- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9c182ed14b1ea1a28cbc56fe71a5a373aca0268` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4707e188297797f5fb4b9bc4cc0bed018c5ced8e` — the merge of head `67d5021948ac82000adfcca2bbde972ffa126eef` into base `c9c182ed14b1ea1a28cbc56fe71a5a373aca0268`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4707e188297797f5fb4b9bc4cc0bed018c5ced8e && git checkout 4707e188297797f5fb4b9bc4cc0bed018c5ced8e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c9c182ed14b1ea1a28cbc56fe71a5a373aca0268 67d5021948ac82000adfcca2bbde972ffa126eef && git checkout -B drift-repro c9c182ed14b1ea1a28cbc56fe71a5a373aca0268 && git merge --no-ff 67d5021948ac82000adfcca2bbde972ffa126eef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9c182ed14b1ea1a28cbc56fe71a5a373aca0268
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c9c182ed14b1ea1a28cbc56fe71a5a373aca0268` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `225de70625bf89045e68b26405891cd6ce2f6d90`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20648 (body; comments 5891790566 triage, 5902376781 claim, 5903382265 and 5903601935 `os-dev-report`); PR #20766 (body, 17-file list, net diff against `main` from merge-base `a6866da0c7`: 17 files, +592/-75); the check-runs on the head. The PR head was still `225de70625` when read.

Check-runs on the head as read for this record: 41 runs — 35 `success`, 5 `skipped` (Auto Label and Check PR Size duplicates, Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke), 1 `in_progress` (`Lint & Repo Gates`). Green include `Check Changeset` (both runs), `Test Core` and all six shards, `TypeScript Type Check`, the four `Type Check` jobs, `Build Core`, the Dogfood gates, `Temporal Conformance`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, and the claim/single-writer guards. Not waited on. The `Test Core` failure on `2c59fcaf18` is the previous head's (shards cancelled by the round-1 push); this head's `Test Core` is `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`MigrationFlagEngine` (`@objectstack/platform-objects/system`, published) — required `find` replaced by required `findOne`: right, and rightly declared BREAKING.** It is the parameter type of six exported helpers — `readDataMigrationFlag`, `isDataMigrationVerified`, `mayActIrreversibly`, `recordDataMigrationRun`, `recordFileColumnMove`, `attestFreshDatastore` (migration-flag.ts:71/120/142/189/258/383 at head) — exactly the six the changeset names. Accept set for a hand-written stand-in: narrowed — one lacking `findOne` stops compiling, and a fresh object literal typed as the interface that still spells `find` fails the excess-property check. The formally widened half (a stand-in need not spell `find`) is unusable against the base and adds no capability. At run time a find-only stand-in's read throws inside `readDataMigrationFlag`'s `try`, the `catch` answers `null`, the gates stay closed — the changeset sentence is true. The new TSDoc ("the one read these helpers make") is true: typecheck green with `find` gone from the type proves no other read remains in that file.
2. **`SeedTenancyLedger` (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`) — same swap: right.** It reaches the public surface only as `SeedTenancySeam.ledger` (`SeedTenancySeam` is the package export; `resolveSeedTenancyLedger` is module-level, not on the package index). What a consumer observes: `resolveSeedTenancySeam(host)` answers `ledger: undefined` for a host with `find` but no `findOne`, and `recordSeedTenancyReceipt` then logs at `warn` that it could not record its receipt (verified at the `if (!ledger)` branch). The docblock enumerating the ledger's readers now says `findOne` — true. Nit for the same changeset edit: the body names `resolveSeedTenancyLedger`, a name no consumer can import; the reachable name is `resolveSeedTenancySeam`.
3. **`@objectstack/objectql` — no published signature moves: right, `patch`.** Three internal readers (`readMigrationFlagVerified`, `recordObservedDeviation`, `retractCreationAttestation`) go through `this.findOne`; no exported type changes. Driver-facing, `sys_migration` now arrives as `driver.findOne`, and both verbs are required `IDataDriver` members. The options survive the move: `where: { id }` is a non-empty predicate so `requireFindOnePredicate` passes, and `context` goes through `mergeReadContext(query.context, options.context)` on both verbs (engine.ts:11323 vs 11595). `SqlDriver.findOne` calls `findRows(object, { ...query, limit: 1 }, options, true)` (sql-driver.ts:7694), so the PR body's H1 sentences are true. No non-test `find(...)` reader of `sys_migration` remains at head.
4. **Transitive: `FilesToReferencesEngine` (`@objectstack/service-storage`) = `BackfillEngine & MigrationFlagEngine` narrows too.** service-storage is not in the changeset front matter. Acceptable, not a defect: every package sits in the `fixed` lockstep group and re-versions together; the BREAKING paragraph names `FilesToReferencesEngine` by package; the compiler error a stand-in author gets names `MigrationFlagEngine`. Recorded so the seat sees the surface.
5. **Engine failure logging on the new path: no regression.** `find` demotes a missing table to `debug` through `reportFindFailure`; `findOne` has no catch of its own and logs nothing, and `readMigrationFlagVerified`'s own `catch` handles the miss. So a first boot gains no engine-level line. The PR body's acceptance note ("the engine's own missing-table line is already demoted to `debug`") describes the old `find` path — imprecise, harmless. The driver's `DATABASE_ERROR` line on a new database's first boot is pre-existing and filed as #20768 (open).
6. **Triage rulings honoured: right.** No `orderBy` added anywhere in the diff; `sql-driver.ts` is not in the file list ("⛔ Not option 2"); the driver's check and wording unchanged.
7. **Pins: met at the seam the ruling names.** `packages/runtime/src/sys-migration-point-lookup.integration.test.ts` runs a real `SqlDriver` over one SQLite file with a second driver instance that never registered the table (precondition asserted: `paginationTieBreaker('sys_migration')` is null), drives the engine's gate read, `readDataMigrationFlag` and the receipt-shaped `findOne` (0 paging warnings), then the control `find('sys_migration', { limit: 1 })` (exactly 1). The 17.4-created-file readings on `objectstack dev` and `os migrate plan` (1 before, 0 after, both builds) are the dev's manual measurement in the PR body; the automated pin sits at the engine/driver seam, not the CLI. The objectql pin covers all three engine readers on their production paths, with a lit probe.
8. **Gate ledgers: right.** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` only grew (new `findOne` rows, `update` pin 3 to 4); `scripts/objectql-double-limit.baseline.json` ratcheted down (3 entries removed, one `blind` 2 to 1). Test doubles now hold to `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`, a tightening.
9. **Shipped prose.** Changeset body sentences checked true: the five readers and their names; the boot-order mechanism; "the driver's check is unchanged"; the six helper names; the run-time behaviour of a find-only stand-in; "ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention for accept-set narrowings" (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, echoed across the current stock). PR body factual sentences true against the code (H1, H3, "what changed", tests named exist). One false sentence sits inside the adr-0087 marker — see ③ and the FAIL item under ②.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/platform-objects` `minor` + BREAKING, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `minor` + BREAKING, `@objectstack/objectql` `patch`: right.** A required member replaced on a published interface is the class `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` names as `major` at GA and `minor` during the launch window; the carriers are the `**BREAKING**` banner and the ADR-0087 disposition, both present. Title carries `!`. The fixed group takes the highest bump for every package, so objectql's `patch` is the honest grade of its own surface and costs nothing.
- **The Clause-② line — `no (narrowing)` rather than `yes (narrowing)`: right.** The value answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」. This diff relaxes no accept set a consumer can use and adds no capability: the swap's only "widening" — a stand-in without `find` is newly accepted — could not have existed against the base type, and nothing an author writes moves. The stock spells `yes (narrowing)` for diffs that also add something usable (20678 accepts disables it used to refuse; 20282 makes two authored keys take effect; 20646 opens new entry paths). `no (narrowing)` is a truthful `no` to the widening question carrying the breaking arm, which is the arm's purpose. PR body line 3 and the changeset agree; the level is `minor` either way.
- **FAIL — the ADR-0087 disposition contradicts its own body.** `runtime-interface-only` is the right category for the *change*: both symbols are published runtime TypeScript interfaces, born outside any Zod/spec/object-definition surface, projections of no schema, referenced by no metadata surface (no `*.zod.ts` or `packages/spec/src/**` file names either), the compiler at the stand-in's call site is the channel — the #8277 shape D7 ratified. `type-surface-only` is rightly excluded (both were concretely typed at base); `unpublished`, `registered`, `already-registered` rightly excluded. But the category's own definition has a fifth condition: ADR-0087 D7 — "It also inherits the `no-migration-prescription` refusal. A body that prescribes a rewrite cannot claim this category either"; D8 — `type-surface-only` "is the **only** category exempt" from that refusal, and the refusal "cannot tell a prescription for a metadata upgrader from a prescription for a source-code consumer". The body's `| Surface | FROM | TO |` table is this repo's FROM/TO pair notation for a migration prescription — the exact framing #18905 (`a5ec0bebe8`) removed from the #18318 changeset to keep the same `runtime-interface-only` claim honest after #18745. So the claim as written stands on a detector miss (the dev says so), which is the #8299 anti-pattern the category was created to close, and the marker sentence "the body does prescribe a rewrite, for TypeScript source rather than stored metadata, which is the shape this category was built for" is false against D7/D8. **Fix (changeset-only, the #18905 move):** keep the category and both path#Symbol refs; replace the FROM/TO table with the consumer's one-line fix in prose — no FROM/TO columns, no arrow, no "migration" label (e.g. "Your fix — a stand-in that implemented `find` for these helpers implements `findOne(object, options)` instead, answering the row whose `where.id` matches or `null`"); rewrite the marker's justification to say the body carries no migration prescription, the stand-in author's fix is compiler-carried. Same edit: name `resolveSeedTenancySeam` where the body says `resolveSeedTenancyLedger`. `Check Changeset` re-judges the changeset on the new head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Producer flag (H1, H3 falsified; landing site extends to `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, 3 sites): answered, right.** The measured producer is `readMigrationFlagVerified` via `haveFileColumnsMoved`, reached at boot before the schema pass registers the table; the two sibling engine reads are the same enumerated reader set the seed-tenancy docblock names, so moving all five keeps that comment true. Producer clause honoured.
- **Sweep stop line (55 hits, 5 moved, 50 left in 13 packages): escalated, right.** The census is AST-based with its blind spots stated (variable-held `where`/`limit`, `top: 1`), lit on both named sites; several remainders are not one-line moves. Carrier none by the seat's ruling; the 50 stay listed in the PR body. Not this PR's.
- **Files outside the claimed surface: answered.** All test doubles, the runtime pin, and the two gate ledgers; no source outside the three packages.
- **`origin/main` merged once (`53650adcfe`), changeset-only patch round (`225de70625`), no force-push: answered.** The net diff against `main` is clean; round 1 changed only the changeset.
- **Out-of-scope finding filed as #20768: answered** (open; the driver's first-boot line, pre-existing).
- **Stale header in `engine-find-missing-table-log-level.test.ts` listing `readMigrationFlagVerified` as a `find` caller: answered.** It is a "what was measured" table from #13273 — history, not a claim about head. Leave it.
- **Dev's "the seat should re-grade if it reads this as a narrowing": answered** — the seat did (round 1); the grade is right (② above).
- **Dev's ADR-0087 doubt ("if the seat reads the inherited refusal as covering a source-code prescription too, no category the gate offers fits"): answered** — the ADR does read it so (D8), but a category still fits: the change is `runtime-interface-only`; the body must drop the pair-notation prescription, as #18905 did. This is the FAIL item.
- **PR opens with `Fixes #20648`, dev offered `Part of` if the card stays open for the sweep: answered** — the seat ruled carrier none for the remainder, so `Fixes` stands.
- **`open_questions`: empty in both reports.** None to answer.
- **Check-runs: `Lint & Repo Gates` was `in_progress` at read; not waited on.**

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20648-migration-flag-point-lookup`
Reviewed-by: `session_01DEvba2nBuD4tWzfq8r8NFY`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
